newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BELGACOM RETIREMENT PLAN TO COST 24/25 BLN BFR.
newsitem.headline: BELGACOM RETIREMENT PLAN TO COST 24/25 BLN BFR.

text.p: An early retirement offer for 6,290 staff at Belgacom -- one of the pillars of its massive restructuring programme -- will cost the Belgian state telephone firm 24 to 25 billion francs.
Spokesman Jan Margot told Belgian news agency Belga on Wednesday an exact amount was not yet known, but the future savings of the operation would exceed the cost.

Danish telecoms group Tele Danmark said on Tuesday first-half results due on August 29 would show a significant one-off charge related to redundancies in Belgacom, in which it has a stake of about 16 percent.
Tele Danmark said the firm had similar accounting practices to U.S. partner Ameritech , which last month announced a charge of $87 million for the Belgacom layoffs.
Ameritech has around a 17 percent holding in the Belgian firm.
The early retirement offer applies to workers from the age of 50 with a minimum of 20 years of service.

The deal guarantees them 75 percent of their last monthly gross salary until the age of 60 -- the age at which workers are legally allowed to claim early retirement -- plus a departure premium based on six months pay.
Belgacom, 49.9 percent owned by a consortium also including Singapore Telecom and three Belgian investors, has total staff of 26,000.
